points.why: It says scrutiny should be set by the decision's domain, not the agent's record, and that the 96% covers only routine clear-domain work.
It calls self-triage the weakest point because the agent answers in a confident analysis-and-recommendation shape, and it has people classify request categories up front instead.
Routine work calls written runbooks, capacity planning is proposed by the agent and checked by a named person, and incidents follow runbooks written in advance.
It describes how trust lowers checking, which lets trust rise further until scrutiny is gone when a high-stakes failure arrives.

pitfalls.why: It refuses the autonomy as stated and limits the 96% to the work it actually covers.
